claims.text: A metadynamics-based processing scheme will enable large-scale reaction between refractory high-entropy alloy and Cu constituents.
Metadynamics-based processing will produce a stable composite microstructure.
The proposed method works by overcoming free-energy barriers associated with positive heats of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
A mesoscale mixture of separate refractory high-entropy alloy and Cu phases naturally tends toward phase separation because of thermodynamic incompatibility.
A metadynamics-enhanced sampling protocol can be applied during physical reaction processing to explore and surmount free-energy barriers.
Controlled thermal annealing may promote the desired reaction pathway when combined with the metadynamics protocol.
The proposed processing should be conducted at high temperature under conditions that include irradiation-related challenges.
The intervention will control and stabilize phase boundaries between refractory intermetallic compounds and a Cu matrix.
Alteration of the free-energy landscape mediates stabilization of the phase boundaries.
Mapping and overcoming barriers arising from endothermic mixing guides the reaction toward reduced deleterious phase separation.
Reduced phase separation produces a composite with enhanced stability and integrated thermal and mechanical properties.
The resulting composite will have a homogeneous, stable microstructure with reduced phase separation.
The resulting composite will have improved mechanical strength while maintaining thermal stability.
Conventional mechanical alloying and standard sintering cannot manage the relevant free-energy barriers.
Conventional processing causes unstable microstructures through uncontrolled phase separation.
Extreme reactor conditions or excessively high free-energy barriers may limit the effectiveness of the proposed method.
